parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the wavelength of a progressive wave.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO) is used to analyse a sound wave. The screen of the CRO is shown in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:figure_5_1}}

Fig. 5.1

The time-base setting of the CRO is $2.5\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$.

Determine the frequency of the sound wave.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem:
The source emitting the sound in (b) is at point A. Waves travel from the source to point C along two different paths, AC and ABC, as shown in Fig. 5.2.

{{figure:figure_5_2}}

Fig. 5.2 (not to scale)

Distance AB is $8.0\text{ m}$ and distance AC is $20.8\text{ m}$. Angle ABC is $90^{\circ}$. Assume that there is no phase change of the sound wave due to the reflection at point B. The wavelength of the waves is $1.6\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Show that the waves meeting at C have a path difference of $6.4\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why an intensity maximum is detected at point C.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the difference between the times taken for the sound to travel from the source to point C along the two different paths.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: The wavelength of the sound is gradually increased. Calculate the wavelength of the sound when an intensity maximum is next detected at point C.
